oneTimers: $156M of restructuring and other charges under Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan — $142M of severance, $11M of litigation charges and $3M of asset impairments; excluded from non-GAAP results. Cumulative plan cost reached $2.9B of an expected ~$3.0B total.
A $(112)M loss on equity investments, net, versus a $205M gain a year ago — mark-to-market moves on Intel's investment portfolio rather than chip sales, a $317M year-over-year swing.

A $94M loss from divestiture: the final close of the NAND sale to SK hynix brought in less than the receivable recorded at the first closing, after a final negotiated settlement; excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $(285)M combines a $(112)M loss on equity investments, net with $(173)M of interest and other, net. Intel recorded a $301M tax provision on a $(586)M pre-tax loss, a (51.4)% GAAP tax rate — tax owed even while losing money.
pngFooterNote: Flat sales and a thin margin produced an $887M loss.

segments.name: Client Computing Group
segments.note: PC and client chips; down 8% YoY. Segment operating income was $2,361M, down from $2,822M a year ago.

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Xeon server chips and AI data-center products; up 8% YoY. Segment operating income was $575M, up from $417M a year ago.

segments.name: Intel Foundry
segments.note: Intel's chip factories, shown at their $31M of sales to OUTSIDE customers only (Q1 2025 10-Q). Foundry's total segment revenue was $4,667M, but $4,636M of that was wafers sold to Intel's own product groups — counting it here would count the same dollars twice. Foundry lost $2,320M in the quarter.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Mobileye (self-driving tech), Altera and smaller businesses. Intel reports this group at $943M; it is shown as $881M here, net of $62M of intersegment eliminations not attributable to Foundry, so the parts sum exactly to Intel's $12,667M total. Up 47% YoY.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Mar 29, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Revenue was flat at $12.7B and R&D plus MG&A fell 19% year over year to $4.8B, but gross margin slid to 36.9% from 41.0%, so Intel still lost money on operations. GAAP EPS was $(0.19); non-GAAP EPS was $0.13.
takeaways.title: Cost cuts weren't enough to save the quarter

takeaways.text: Intel Foundry lost $2,320M on $4,667M of segment revenue, and only $31M of that revenue came from outside customers — the rest was wafers sold to Intel's own product groups. Client Computing still earned $2,361M and Data Center and AI earned $575M.
takeaways.title: Foundry lost far more than the whole company

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $813M, but after $6.2B of gross capital spending, adjusted free cash flow was $(3,680)M. New CEO Lip-Bu Tan cut the 2025 operating-expense target to ~$17B (and ~$16B for 2026) and gross capex to $18B; Q2 guidance is $11.2–12.4B of revenue with GAAP EPS of $(0.32). Intel also agreed to sell 51% of Altera to Silver Lake.
takeaways.title: Cash burned while the new CEO resets the plan

verdict: Intel lost $887 million in the first quarter as flat revenue of $12.7 billion met a thinner 36.9% gross margin, and its chip factories alone lost $2.3 billion while a new CEO moved to cut costs and spending.
